T.R. Ramachandran Nair, J.

The prayers made by the petitioner in this company petition are as follows:
(a) This Hon'ble Court may be pleased to pass orders for the declaration that all the affairs of the Malayalam Industries Company Limited should be investigated by competent Inspector to be appointed in this behalf by the Central Government under Section 237(a) under the provisions of the Companies Act, 1956; and (b) Grant such other or further relief as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and necessary in the circumstance of this case.
2. We heard Sri.N. Dharmadan, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri.
Vakkom N. Vijayan, the learned counsel appearing for respondents 2 and 3 and the learned Assistant Solicitor General Sri. N. Nagaresh for the first respondent.
3.

The learned senior counsel Sri.N. Dharmadan submitted that in the light of the mediation settlement agreement between the parties, appropriate follow up action has to be taken by the first respondent for conducting an inspection into the affairs of the second respondent by appointing Registrar of Companies or any other inspectors.
The learned counsel for respondents 2 and 3 has no objection for the said course also.
The mediation settlement agreement has been produced as Annexure III along with C.A.No.171 of 2015 in this company petition.
We have disposed today by a common judgment in Comp.Appeals Nos.3 and 4 of 2014 by recording the settlement.
Clause 1 of the settlement, is the one agreed to by both sides to have an inspection into all affairs of the 2nd respondent.
In that view of the matter, we issue a direction as sought for.
The first respondent will have to take appropriate action in the matter.

For enabling the first respondent to pass appropriate orders, the petitioner will furnish a copy of this judgment along with the judgment in Comp. Appeals Nos.3 and 4 of 2014, along with a proper representation.
On receipt of the same, appropriate action will have to be taken by the first respondent.
The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner, requested that the first respondent may be directed to take appropriate action within a time limit.

We direct the first Thomas George vs Union Of India on 2 September, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109855896/
3 respondent to see that effective action is taken within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment and the representation from the petitioner.
